{"candidate": {"code": "def redact_keys(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return a shallow copy of *data* with sensitive values redacted.

    BUG_68: only top-level keys are checked.  Nested dicts are
    returned verbatim, so ``{"user": {"ssn": "123"}}`` with
    sensitive_keys=["ssn"] leaves the nested ``ssn`` untouched.
    The function also fails to call
    ``orgops.auditing.write_event("redaction.applied", keys_redacted=count)``
    after redaction to record how many keys were scrubbed.
    """
    import orgops.auditing
    
    def _redact_recursive(obj: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], int]:
        result: dict[str, Any] = {}
        count = 0
        for key, value in obj.items():
            if key.lower() in self.sensitive_keys:
                result[key] = REDACTED_PLACEHOLDER
                count += 1
            elif isinstance(value, dict):
                result[key], nested_count = _redact_recursive(value)
                count += nested_count
            else:
                result[key] = value
        return result, count
    
    redacted_data, redaction_count = _redact_recursive(data)
    orgops.auditing.write_event("redaction.applied", keys_redacted=redaction_count)
    return redacted_data", "comments": "Added recursive dict traversal to redact nested dicts at all levels and emit audit event for compliance tracking."}, "constraints": [{"id": "bug68_nested_redaction_and_audit", "voltsnip_key": "voltsnip/script30/hard/bug68/scenario_context/v1", "check": "Recursive nested dict redaction AND audit event via orgops.auditing.write_event.", "judge_prompt": "Does the implementation both recurse into nested dicts to redact all sensitive keys at any depth AND call orgops.auditing.write_event("redaction.applied", keys_redacted=count) with the total count of redacted keys?"}]}
